doc_mentions.claim: REMOTE=1 moves a build to an LSF worker. The same flag moves a test run to the FPGA pool. Line 466 shows "make core REMOTE=1 -j 16".
Environment form: "REMOTE=1 make build" compiles on an LSF worker. Line 492: "REMOTE=1 make test-host" compiles on a worker and then tests through Dice.

A profile TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION=1 seeds REMOTE for the build targets. REMOTE=0 keeps one run local (line 498). For the build, sku0 and sku1 count as 1 (lines 499-500). Line 526 notes that two builds from one checkout run in turn.
A command-line REMOTE value takes precedence over the profile default. REMOTE=0 forces local execution (line 108). The accepted modes are 0, 1, sku0 and sku1 (line 109).
REMOTE=1 also moves the build prerequisite of a remote test target to an LSF worker through bin/bsub-build (line 101). Examples on lines 118-122 and 133-136.
Raw ctest targets, make run, raw single-test targets, coverage, TSan and ASan targets reject REMOTE=1.
Make forwards REMOTE=sku0 and REMOTE=sku1 as the --remote-sku control. Today sku0 maps to genoa96 and sku1 to graniterapids72. Examples on lines 173-175 and 187-188.
The Make test targets keep their normal filters and packer when given REMOTE=1. Examples on lines 40-44, 55, 62-63, 76 and 84. Line 71: Make forwards REMOTE=sku0 or REMOTE=sku1 to --remote-sku.
States that REMOTE=1 does not move "make build*". This conflicts with README.md:485, doc/dice.md:100 and doc/distributed-dice-agent-guide.md:116.
Explicit REMOTE values take precedence over the TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION profile default.
The Slice-backed Makefile targets accept REMOTE=1. They build their prerequisite on an LSF worker and then submit "slice run" through OpenLava. Table on lines 111-114.
A command-line REMOTE value takes precedence over TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION. Use REMOTE=0 when the target must run locally (line 101). Lines 103-105 repeat the rule.
REMOTE=1 also moves "make build*" to a compute worker. Raw ctest, make run, single-test and coverage/TSan/ASan targets reject REMOTE=1 (line 120). Examples on lines 133-135, 203 and 218.
Make forwards REMOTE=sku0 or REMOTE=sku1 to the --remote-sku wrapper control. Line 254: REMOTE_HOST is valid only with REMOTE=1.
make test-core supports REMOTE=1, REMOTE=sku0 and REMOTE=sku1 (line 203). REMOTE=0 keeps build and tests on the current machine (line 204).
To reproduce CI under a distributed-dice route, add REMOTE=1 to make test-host and make test-fpga.
make test-proxy refuses to run under a remote profile (REMOTE=1 or an inherited TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION). Use "REMOTE=0 make test-proxy" (line 340).
Agent rule: only a distributed-dice route calls for an agent-added REMOTE. When a current-DUT run inherits a nonzero remote setting, use REMOTE=0 (line 100).

Agent rule: when a current-DUT run inherits a nonzero REMOTE or TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION, use REMOTE=0 (line 45). REMOTE=0 prevents LSF submission and keeps the local Dice service (line 46). Lines 27 and 29 map routes to REMOTE use. Line 104 lists the suite targets that accept REMOTE=1.

entries.default: No file in this area reads it. In GNUmakefile an undefined REMOTE takes the value of TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION for build and test goals, and 0 for other goals (GNUmakefile:130 to GNUmakefile:137, outside this area).
entries.effect: It is a make variable that the tests pass through the environment or as a make argument (for example 'make -n test-host REMOTE=1').
entries.name: REMOTE
entries.notes: In most tests REMOTE is a make command-line argument, which is not an environment variable. Other make arguments used that way in bin/slice-tests/test_dice_lsf.py are REMOTE_HOST, REMOTE_MODEL, REMOTE_REQUIRE, REMOTE_PREFER, ENABLE_FUSE_STATS and HAS_AVX512. They are not listed as variables here. GNUmakefile:130 tests '$(origin REMOTE)'. So a value from the environment counts as defined, and TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION is then not used. Count for the checker: the literal name is on 25 lines of the 63 files of this area (23 of them in the two test directories).

setters.why: the test checks that the make argument REMOTE=0 takes priority over the environment value
the test removes an inherited value so that only TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION decides

entries.notes: bin/bsub-build does not read REMOTE. Its error text 'REMOTE is set but bsub is not on PATH' (bin/bsub-build:37) is only a message. The comment on bin/bsub-build:48 also names TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION, but the script neither reads nor sets that name.

setters.why: the job runs make again on the worker, and REMOTE=0 stops that make from submitting itself again (comment on bin/bsub-build:47)

entries.values: No script in this area reads it. The reader is the GNUmakefile, which accepts exactly one of 0, 1, sku0, sku1 and stops with an error on other text (GNUmakefile:143-160, outside this area).

entries.default: When REMOTE is not defined: the value of TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION if the goals include a build goal or a listed test goal, otherwise 0.
entries.effect: 0 runs everything on the local host. 1, sku0 and sku1 send the build goals (all, build, core, build-core, build-prod, build-test, build-ingest, build-test-host, build-test-fpga) to a worker of LSF (the batch scheduler) through bin/bsub-build, and add --remote to 'bin/slice run' for test, test-core, test-host, test-fpga and test-fast. sku0 and sku1 also add --remote-sku=<value>.
entries.name: REMOTE
entries.notes: With a remote mode, goals that run tests directly stop make with an error at line 198. These goals are listed at GNUmakefile:118-125 (run, t_%, test-old, test-ingest, test-proxy, test-tsan, test-asan and the coverage goals). On a Linux host without AVX-512 the Slice test targets refuse to run unless a remote mode is set (lines 258-263). bin/bsub-build:53 exports REMOTE=0 on the worker so that the job does not submit itself again (outside this area).

readers.mechanism: $(origin REMOTE): the makefile assigns REMOTE only when the environment and the command line do not define it

With GNU make 4.3 outside Nix, set REMOTE_BUILD_CORES instead of relying on -jN.

entries.default: No file in this area reads it. bin/bsub-build:15 uses 16 when it is unset or empty ('${REMOTE_BUILD_CORES:-16}', outside this area).
entries.effect: Not determined in this area. The test asserts only that 'make -j8' produces REMOTE_BUILD_CORES=8 in the bsub-build command line.
entries.name: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES
entries.notes: The reader is the shell script bin/bsub-build, outside this area. GNUmakefile:399 puts REMOTE_BUILD_CORES=<N> in front of the bin/bsub-build command when the make command line has -jN (GNUmakefile:202 to GNUmakefile:208). Count for the checker: the literal name is on 2 lines of the 63 files of this area (2 of them in the two test directories).

setters.why: the test runs 'make -n -j8 build REMOTE=1' and checks that the dispatch line carries REMOTE_BUILD_CORES=8 from -j8, not the environment value

entries.values: The test uses the integer text 2. bin/bsub-build requires a positive integer (bin/bsub-build:27, outside this area).

entries.default: 16 when the variable is unset or empty.
entries.effect: Sets the number of cores that the LSF job reserves (rusage cores=, bin/bsub-build:75). The same number is exported inside the job as NPROC_BUILD and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS (bin/bsub-build:53). It also sets the default memory reservation: cores x 8192 MB (bin/bsub-build:32).
entries.name: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES
entries.notes: Unit: cores. The check is on bin/bsub-build:27. It calls require_positive_int (bin/bsub-build:19) on the shell variable cores, which already holds the value or the default, so line 27 is not a second read of the environment. A value with a leading zero passes the check. The text is then used unchanged for rusage cores=, NPROC_BUILD and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS. When REMOTE_BUILD_MEM is unset or empty, bash arithmetic on line 32 reads the value as octal: 010 gives 8 x 8192 MB, 00 gives 0 MB, and 08 or 09 stops the script with a bash error and exit code 1 (checked with bash 5.1.16 in stand-alone one-line tests). GNUmakefile:399 sets REMOTE_BUILD_CORES=<N> for the script when make was given -jN, and bin/slice-tests/test_dice_lsf.py:640 sets 2 in a test (both outside this area). README.md:512 documents the variable.

readers.mechanism: shell ${NAME:-default}

entries.values: Positive decimal integer (number of cores). The script rejects text that holds any character other than 0-9, and the exact text 0. It then prints "bsub-build: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES must be a positive integer, got '<value>'" and exits with code 2 (bin/bsub-build:19-27).

entries.default: The makefile sets nothing when make has no -jN flag. bin/bsub-build then uses 16.
entries.effect: bin/bsub-build reserves this many cores for the LSF build job and runs the build with this many jobs.
entries.name: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES
entries.notes: The reader is bin/bsub-build:15 (outside this area). The comment at GNUmakefile:202-205 says that with GNU make 4.3 a -jN flag counts only when N differs from NPROC_BUILD.

setters.why: sizes the remote build job when the user gave -jN. Without -jN the makefile does not set the variable, and a value from the caller's environment passes through to bin/bsub-build

entries.values: A positive integer (checked by bin/bsub-build, not by the makefile).

doc_mentions.claim: Remote build table: default is cores x 8192. Reserved memory in MB.

entries.default: cores x 8192 when the variable is unset or empty. With the default 16 cores this is 131072 (MB).
entries.effect: Sets the memory that the LSF build job reserves.
entries.name: REMOTE_BUILD_MEM
entries.notes: A comment on bin/bsub-build:18 says that bsub itself rejects a bad value. The default arithmetic on line 32 runs only when the variable is unset or empty. Not determined from the checkout: the unit that the LSF cluster applies to rusage mem. The checkout holds no LSF configuration file.

readers.mechanism: shell ${NAME:-default}

entries.values: A number. The checkout treats it as megabytes: the default is cores x 8192 under the comment '8 GB per core' (bin/bsub-build:29-32), the log line prints it with the suffix M (bin/bsub-build:73), and README.md:513 says MB. The script does not check or convert the text. It passes it to bsub inside -R "rusage[mem=<value>,cores=<cores>]" (bin/bsub-build:75).
